title: Army-issued Boehm clarinet versus his Albert system
summary: Why he kept his larger-bore Albert clarinet, its volume next to George Lewis's band, and carrying two instruments in service.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: You had trouble with that bane system clarinet.
Well, the Army issued me a bane. So I couldn't play a bane, so I had to carry two clarinet. I had my own, yeah.
So you used your old albert then?
Yes, but I was charged with a bane. So I had to carry a long two clarinet.

What is your opinion of the difference of the two? Is there much difference in tone? Why do you like the albert? Of course you learned on that, so it's easier for you. But if you had your choice to start on either one of them, which would you pick now?

Well, I noticed that so many clarinet players that I found in the albert and I looked at them, the boar in the albert is much larger than the boar in the bane clarinet. And there's more volume. I can get more volume. I can play just another clarinet player and you can't hardly hear them. Well, Dixieland music, like when this band from New Orleans was out here, this George Lewis band, they play awful strong.
Well, I could be heard with them.
He played with them. I know, yeah. Darman Pierce told me about it. Yeah.
So that's the difference I find.

Do you think you can do more with it? That is, the clarinet, by not having as many keys, does it seem more like it's a part of you that is your fingering? Is there much difference in your fingering? It's the difference in the fingering, yes.
That's what I found. You've never played the bane enough, I guess,
to really get used to it. No, no, I couldn't make it.
To feel how it would feel to play it.
And after I figured I got up in the eight and then the music business got slow and I had to go to work again, I said, well, no need to try and switch. And I'll just stay on that.
